title.zh: 卷三百五十七 列傳第一百十六 何灌 李熙靖 王雲 譚世勣 梅執禮 程振 劉延慶
title.en: Volume 357 Biographies 116: He Guan, Li Xijing, Wang Yun, Tan Shiji, Mei Zhili, Cheng Zhen, Liu Yanqing
title.raw: 卷三百五十七 列傳第一百十六 何灌 李熙靖 王雲 譚世勣 梅執禮 程振 劉延慶 Volume 357 Biographies 116: He Guan, Li Xijing, Wang Yun, Tan Shiji, Mei Zhili, Cheng Zhen, Liu Yanqing

sentences.zh: 何灌 李熙靖 王雲 譚世勣 梅執禮 程振 劉延慶

translations.literal: He Guan, Li Xijing, Wang Yun, Tan Shiji, Mei Zhili, Cheng Zhen, Liu Yanqing
translations.idiomatic: He Guan, Li Xijing, Wang Yun, Tan Shiji, Mei Zhili, Cheng Zhen, and Liu Yanqing

sentences.zh: 何灌，字仲源，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: He Guan, styled Zhongyuan, was a man of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He Guan, courtesy name Zhongyuan, was a native of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 武選登第，為河東從事。

translations.literal: He passed the military selection examination and served as an aide in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the military civil-service examination and became an aide in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 經略使韓縝雖數試其材，而常沮抑之，不假借。

translations.literal: The frontier commissioner Han Zhen, though he tested his talent several times, always held him back and did not lend him support.
translations.idiomatic: Although the frontier commissioner Han Zhen repeatedly tested his abilities, he constantly held Guan back and gave him no backing.

sentences.zh: 久乃語之曰：「君奇士也，他日當據吾坐。」

translations.literal: After a long while he said to him: "You are an extraordinary man; someday you will take my seat."
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Han told him, "You are an extraordinary man; one day you will sit in my chair."

sentences.zh: 為府州、火山軍巡檢。

translations.literal: He was made inspector of Fuzhou and the Huoshan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was appointed inspector of Fuzhou and the Huoshan Army.

sentences.zh: 盜蘇延福狡悍，為二邊患，灌親梟其首。

translations.literal: The bandit Su Yanfu was crafty and fierce and a menace on both borders; Guan personally beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Su Yanfu was cunning and fierce and plagued both frontiers; Guan personally took his head.

sentences.zh: 賈胡疃有泉，遼人常越境而汲，灌親申畫界堠，遏其來，忿而舉兵犯我。

translations.literal: At Jiahu Tan there was a spring; Liao people often crossed the border to draw water. Guan personally planned and set up border markers to stop them; angered, they raised troops to invade us.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiahu Tan there was a spring that Liao subjects often crossed the border to use. Guan personally laid out and marked the boundary to block them; enraged, they raised an army and attacked our territory.

sentences.zh: 灌迎高射之，發輒中，或著崖石皆沒鏃，敵驚以為神，逡巡斂去。

translations.literal: Guan met them from high ground and shot; every shot hit, and some buried in cliff rock up to the fletching; the enemy feared him as divine and withdrew hesitantly.
translations.idiomatic: Guan met them from higher ground and shot; every arrow struck, and some buried in cliff rock to the fletching. The enemy took him for a god and withdrew after hesitating.

sentences.zh: 後三十年，契丹蕭太師與灌會，道曩事，數何巡檢神射，灌曰：「即灌是也。」

translations.literal: Thirty years later the Khitan Grand Preceptor Xiao met with Guan and recalled old affairs, asking several times about Inspector He's divine archery. Guan said: "That was I."
translations.idiomatic: Thirty years later the Khitan Grand Preceptor Xiao met Guan and spoke of old times, repeatedly asking about Inspector He's miraculous shooting. Guan said, "That was I."

sentences.zh: 蕭矍然起拜。

translations.literal: Xiao started up in alarm and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao started up in alarm and bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 為河東將，與夏人遇，鐵騎來追，灌射皆徹甲，至洞胸出背，疊貫後騎，羌懼而引卻。

translations.literal: As a Hedong general he encountered the Xia; iron cavalry pursued; Guan's shots all pierced armor, some through the chest and out the back, stacking through rear riders; the Qiang feared and drew back.
translations.idiomatic: As a Hedong general he met the Xia; iron cavalry pursued him, and every shot Guan loosed pierced armor—some through the chest and out the back, skewering riders behind as well. The Qiang were terrified and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 知甯化軍、豐州，徙熙河都監，見童貫不拜，貫憾焉。

translations.literal: He became prefect of Ninghua Army and Fengzhou, transferred to Xida River superintendent; when he met Tong Guan he did not bow, and Guan resented this.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Ninghua Army and Fengzhou, then was transferred to superintendent of the Xida River circuit. When he met Tong Guan he did not bow, and Tong resented it.

sentences.zh: 張康國薦于徽宗，召對，問西北邊事，以笏畫禦榻，指坐衣花紋為形勢。

translations.literal: Zhang Kangguo recommended him to Emperor Huizong; called to audience, asked about northwest frontier affairs; he used his tablet to draw on the imperial couch and pointed to patterns on the seated robe as terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kangguo recommended him to Emperor Huizong. Summoned for audience, Guan was questioned on northwest frontier affairs; he traced on the imperial couch with his tablet and used the patterns on the emperor's robe to illustrate the terrain.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「敵在吾目中矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The enemy is within my eyes."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The enemy is plain before my eyes."

sentences.zh: 提點河東刑獄，遷西上閣門使、領威州刺史、知滄州。

translations.literal: Judicial intendant of Hedong; promoted to West Upper Inner Gate Commissioner, acting Weizhou prefect, and Cangzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was judicial intendant of Hedong, then promoted to West Upper Inner Gate Commissioner, acting prefect of Weizhou, and prefect of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以治城鄣功，轉引進使。

translations.literal: For merit in governing walls and forts, he was transferred to Commissioner for Promotion of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: For his work repairing walls and fortifications, he was promoted to Commissioner for Promotion of Merit.

sentences.zh: 詔運粟三十萬石於並塞三州，灌言：「水淺不勝舟，陸當用車八千乘，沿邊方登麥，願以運費增價就糴之。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered transport of three hundred thousand shi of grain to three prefectures on the Bian frontier. Guan said: "The water is shallow and cannot bear boats; by land eight thousand carts should be used. Along the frontier wheat is just sprouting; I wish to use the transport fees to add to the price and buy grain locally."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered three hundred thousand shi of grain shipped to three frontier prefectures on the Bian line. Guan argued, "The water is too shallow for boats; overland would require eight thousand carts. Wheat is just coming up along the border—I ask that the transport costs be used instead to buy grain on the spot at a premium."

sentences.zh: 奏上，報可。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the court, and the proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 安撫使忌之，劾雲板築未畢而冒賞，奪所遷官，仍再貶秩，罷去。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner envied him, impeached that cloud boards and fortifications were not finished yet he claimed reward, stripped the office to which he had been promoted, demoted him in rank again, and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commissioner, jealous of him, impeached him for claiming rewards before the cloud-board fortifications were finished. Guan was stripped of his latest promotion, demoted again in rank, and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知岷州，引邈川水溉間田千頃，湟人號廣利渠。

translations.literal: Before long he became prefect of Minzhou, led Miaochuan water to irrigate a thousand qing of dry land; Qinghai people called it the Broad Benefit Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was prefect of Minzhou. He diverted Miaochuan water to irrigate a thousand qing of dry fields; the people of Huang called the project the Broad Benefit Canal.

sentences.zh: 徙河州，復守岷，提舉熙河蘭湟弓箭手。

translations.literal: Transferred to Hezhou, again defended Min, and supervised the Xida River, Lan, and Huang archer militia.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hezhou, then returned to hold Minzhou and was put in charge of the Xida River, Lan, and Huang archer militia.

sentences.zh: 入言：「漢金城、湟中谷斛八錢，今西寧、湟、廓即其地也，漢、唐故渠尚可考。

translations.literal: He entered court and said: "In Han times Jincheng and Huangzhong had grain at eight cash per hu; today Xining, Huang, and Kuo are that land; Han and Tang old canals can still be traced.
translations.idiomatic: He went to court and said, "Under the Han, Jincheng and Huangzhong sold grain at eight cash per hu; present-day Xining, Huang, and Kuo occupy that same ground, and the old Han and Tang canals can still be traced.

sentences.zh: 若先葺渠引水，使田不病旱，則人樂應募，而射士之額足矣。」

translations.literal: If we first repair the canals to draw water so the fields suffer no drought, then people will gladly enlist and the archer quotas will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: If we first repair the canals and bring in water so the fields are spared drought, people will gladly enlist and the archer quotas will be filled."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 甫半歲，得善田二萬六千頃，募士七千四百人，為他路最。

translations.literal: In only half a year he obtained good fields of twenty-six thousand qing and recruited seven thousand four hundred soldiers—the highest among circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In only half a year he brought under cultivation twenty-six thousand qing of good land and recruited seventy-four hundred men—the highest figure in any circuit.

sentences.zh: 童貫用兵西邊，灌取古骨龍馬進武軍，加吉州防禦使，改知蘭州。

translations.literal: When Tong Guan campaigned on the western border, Guan took ancient Gulong horses to advance the Wujun Army, was added Jizhou defense commissioner, and changed to Lanzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Guan campaigned in the west, Guan seized Gulong horses of antiquity for the Wujun Army, was made defense commissioner of Jizhou, and was reassigned as prefect of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 又攻仁多泉城，炮傷足不顧，卒拔城，斬首五百級。

translations.literal: He also attacked Renduo Spring city; a cannon wounded his foot but he paid no heed; he finally took the city and cut off five hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked Renduo Spring city. A cannon ball wounded his foot, but he ignored it, finally stormed the city, and took five hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 尋改廓州防禦使。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Kuo prefect defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made defense commissioner of Kuo prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宣和初，劉法陷於敵，震武危甚，熙帥劉仲武使灌往救。

translations.literal: Early in the Xuanhe era Liu Fa was trapped by the enemy and Zhenwu was in grave danger; the Xida commander Liu Zhongwu sent Guan to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuanhe era Liu Fa was trapped by the enemy and Zhenwu was in grave peril; the Xida commander Liu Zhongwu sent Guan to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 灌以眾寡不敵，但張虛聲駭之，夏人宵遁。

translations.literal: Guan, with numbers unmatched, only spread false sounds to terrify them; the Xia fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, Guan only spread false alarms to frighten them, and the Xia withdrew by night.

sentences.zh: 灌恐覘其實，遽反兵，仲武猶奏其逗遛，罷為淮西鈐轄。

translations.literal: Guan feared they would spy out the truth and hurriedly turned the army back; Zhongwu still memorialized his delay and he was dismissed to Huaixi command.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the enemy would discover the truth, Guan hurriedly turned his army about. Zhongwu still reported him for stalling, and he was demoted to Huaixi command.

sentences.zh: 從平方臘，獲賊帥呂師囊，遷同州觀察使、浙東都鈐轄，改浙西。

translations.literal: He followed in suppressing Fang La, captured the bandit chief Lu Shinai, was promoted to Tongzhou observation commissioner and Zhedong overall commander, then changed to Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in suppressing Fang La, captured the rebel leader Lu Shinai, was made observation commissioner of Tongzhou and overall commander of eastern Zhe, then transferred to western Zhe.

sentences.zh: 童貫北征，檄統制兵馬，涿、易平，以知易州，遷甯武軍承宣使、燕山路副都總管，又加龍、神衛都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Tong Guan marched north he was ordered to command the troops; Zhuo and Yi were pacified; he became Yi prefect, was promoted to Ningwu Army commissioner and Yan Mountain Route deputy overall commander, and was also made commander of the Dragon and Divine Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On Tong Guan's northern campaign Guan was ordered to take overall command of the forces. Zhuo and Yi were pacified; he became prefect of Yi, was promoted to commissioner of the Ningwu Army and deputy overall commander of the Yan Mountain route, and was also made commander of the Dragon and Divine Guard.

sentences.zh: 夔離不取景州，圍薊州。

translations.literal: Aguda did not take Jingzhou but besieged Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Aguda bypassed Jingzhou and besieged Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 貫諉以兵事，即復景城，釋薊圍。

translations.literal: Guan blamed this on military affairs, immediately recovered Jing city, and lifted the siege of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Guan took responsibility for the military situation, quickly recovered Jing city, and lifted the siege of Ji.

sentences.zh: 郭藥師統蕃、漢兵，灌白：「頃年折氏歸朝，朝廷別置一司，專部漢兵，至於克行，乃許同營。

translations.literal: Guo Yaoshi commanded fan and Han troops. Guan told him: "In recent years when the Zhe clan submitted to the court, the court separately established an office specifically to command Han troops; only at Kexing were they allowed in the same camp.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yaoshi commanded both tribal and Han troops. Guan told him, "When the Zhe clan submitted in earlier years, the court set up a separate office to command Han troops alone; only under Kexing were the two allowed to camp together.

sentences.zh: 今但宜令藥師主常勝軍，而以漢兵委灌輩。」

translations.literal: Now it is fitting only to let Yaoshi command the Ever-Victorious Army and entrust the Han troops to Guan and his colleagues."
translations.idiomatic: Now Yaoshi should command only the Ever-Victorious Army, and the Han troops should be entrusted to me and my colleagues."

sentences.zh: 貫不聽。

translations.literal: Tong Guan would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan would not listen.

sentences.zh: 召還，管幹步軍司。

translations.literal: Recalled, he managed the Infantry Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he took charge of the Infantry Bureau.

sentences.zh: 陪遼使射玉津園，一發破的，再發則否。

translations.literal: Accompanying Liao envoys shooting at Jade Ford Garden, his first shot hit the target; the second did not.
translations.idiomatic: While accompanying Liao envoys at archery in Jade Ford Garden, his first shot struck the target; the second did not.

sentences.zh: 客曰：「太尉不能耶？」

translations.literal: A guest said: "Cannot the Grand Marshal?"
translations.idiomatic: A guest asked, "Cannot the Grand Marshal do it?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「非也，以禮讓客耳。」

translations.literal: He said: "Not so; I yield courtesy to the guest."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "No—I was simply yielding the honor to our guest."

sentences.zh: 整弓復中之，觀者誦歎，帝親賜酒勞之。

translations.literal: He strung the bow again and hit; viewers praised in admiration, and the emperor personally bestowed wine to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: He strung his bow again and hit the mark. The onlookers exclaimed in admiration, and the emperor personally bestowed wine to reward him.

sentences.zh: 遷步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: He was promoted to deputy commander of the Infantry.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy commander of the Infantry.

sentences.zh: 金師南下，悉出禁旅付梁方平守黎陽。

translations.literal: Jin armies marched south; all palace guards were given to Liang Fangping to defend Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin armies marched south, the entire palace guard was sent out under Liang Fangping to hold Liyang.

sentences.zh: 灌謂宰相白時中曰：「金人傾國遠至，其鋒不可當。

translations.literal: Guan told the chief minister Bai Shizhong: "The Jin have mobilized the whole nation and come from afar; their edge cannot be resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Guan told the chief minister Bai Shizhong, "The Jin have thrown the whole kingdom into this expedition from far away; their momentum cannot be withstood.

sentences.zh: 今方平掃精銳以北，萬有一不枝梧，何以善吾後，盍留以衛根本。」

translations.literal: Now Fangping sweeps the elite north; if by any chance they are not sustained, how can we protect our rear? Why not retain them to guard the foundation?"
translations.idiomatic: Fangping is now sweeping our best troops north. If they should fail to hold, how will we secure our rear? We ought to keep a force here to guard the capital itself."

sentences.zh: 不從，明日，又命灌行，辭以軍不堪戰，強之，拜武泰軍節度使、河東河北制置副使。

translations.literal: They did not follow this. The next day he was again ordered to go; he declined on the ground that the army was unfit for battle but was forced; he was appointed Wutai Army commissioner and Hedong-Hebei deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: They did not listen. The next day Guan was ordered out again; he pleaded that his troops were unfit to fight but was overruled and appointed military commissioner of the Wutai Army and deputy commissioner for Hedong and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 未及行而帝內禪，灌領兵入衛。

translations.literal: Before he could depart the emperor abdicated internally; Guan led troops to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could set out the emperor abdicated; Guan led his troops in to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 鄆王楷至門欲入，灌曰：「大事已定，王何所受命而來？」

translations.literal: The Prince of Yun, Cai, came to the gate wishing to enter. Guan said: "The great matter is already settled; from whom does Your Highness receive orders to come?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yun Cai came to the gate wishing to enter. Guan said, "The succession is already settled—under whose orders does Your Highness come?"

sentences.zh: 導者懼而退。

translations.literal: The guide feared and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's attendants, alarmed, withdrew.

sentences.zh: 灌竟行，援兵二萬不能足，聽募民充數。

translations.literal: Guan eventually went; reinforcements of twenty thousand could not be filled, and he was permitted to recruit civilians to fill the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Guan set out after all. He could not muster the promised twenty thousand reinforcements and was allowed to recruit civilians to fill the ranks.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年正月二日，次滑州，方平南奔，灌亦望風迎潰。

translations.literal: On the second day of the first month of the first year of Jingkang he halted at Huazhou; Fangping fled south and Guan also, at the sight of the wind, joined the rout.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the first month of Jingkang 1 he encamped at Huazhou. Fangping fled south, and Guan too broke and ran at the first sign of defeat.

sentences.zh: 黃河南岸無一人禦敵，金師遂直叩京城。

translations.literal: On the south bank of the Yellow River not a man resisted the enemy; the Jin armies went straight to knock at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Not a man on the south bank of the Yellow River stood to oppose them, and the Jin armies marched straight on the capital.

sentences.zh: 灌至，乞入見，不許，而令控守西隅。

translations.literal: When Guan arrived he begged an audience but was not permitted; he was ordered instead to hold the western corner.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan reached the city he begged an audience but was refused and ordered to hold the western sector.

sentences.zh: 背城拒戰凡三日，被創，沒於陣，年六十二。

translations.literal: With his back to the city he resisted battle for three days in all, was wounded, and died in the battle line at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: With the city at his back he fought for three days, was wounded, and fell in battle at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 帳下韓綜、雷彥興，奇士也，各手殺數人，從以死。

translations.literal: Under his tent Han Zong and Lei Yanxing, extraordinary men, each personally killed several men and followed him in death.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zong and Lei Yanxing under his command were men of rare valor; each killed several enemies with his own hand and died with him.

sentences.zh: 欽宗哀悼，賜金帛，命官護葬。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong mourned him, bestowed gold and silk, and ordered officials to escort the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong mourned him, granted gold and silk, and ordered officials to escort his burial.

sentences.zh: 已而言者論其不守河津，追削官秩。

translations.literal: Later critics argued that he had not held the river crossings and posthumously stripped his ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Later critics charged that he had failed to hold the river crossings, and his ranks were posthumously stripped.

sentences.zh: 長子薊，至閣門宣贊舍人。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ji rose to Gate Proclamation Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ji rose to the post of Gate Proclamation Attendant.

sentences.zh: 從父戰，箭貫左臂，拔出之，病創死。

translations.literal: Following his father in battle, an arrow pierced his left arm; he pulled it out and died of the wound.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at his father's side; an arrow pierced his left arm. He pulled it out and died of the wound.

sentences.zh: 紹興四年，中子蘚以灌事泣訴於朝，詔復履正大夫、忠正軍承宣使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxing his middle son Xian wept and petitioned the court on Guan's affair; an edict restored Left Vice Minister of Works rank and loyal upright army commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 4 his middle son Xian wept before the court over his father's case; an edict restored Guan's ranks as Left Vice Minister of Works and commissioner of the Loyal and Upright Army.

sentences.zh: 李熙靖

translations.literal: Li Xijing
translations.idiomatic: Li Xijing

sentences.zh: 李熙靖，字子安，常州晉陵人，唐衛公德裕九世孫也。

translations.literal: Li Xijing, styled Zi'an, was a man of Jinling in Changzhou, ninth-generation descendant of Tang Duke of Wei Li Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xijing, courtesy name Zi'an, was a native of Jinling in Changzhou and a ninth-generation descendant of the Tang Duke of Wei, Li Deyu.

sentences.zh: 祖均、父公弼皆進士第。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jun and father Gongbi both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jun and his father Gongbi had both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 公弼，崇甯初通判潞州，以議三舍法不便，使者劾其沮格詔令，坐削黜以死。

translations.literal: Gongbi, early in Chongning, was vice-prefect of Luzhou; for arguing that the Three Colleges law was inconvenient, an envoy impeached him for obstructing the edict, and he was demoted and died in disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi, early in the Chongning era, was vice-prefect of Luzhou. He argued that the Three Colleges law was unworkable; an envoy impeached him for obstructing imperial orders, and he was stripped of office and died in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 熙靖擢第，又中詞學兼茂，選為辟雍錄、太學正，升博士。

translations.literal: Xijing passed the examination, also passed the erudite literary examination, was selected as Imperial Academy recorder and director of the National University, and was promoted to erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Xijing passed the civil examination and also the erudite literary examination, was appointed recorder of the Imperial Academy and director of the National University, and was promoted to erudite.

sentences.zh: 以父老丐外，除提舉淮東學事便養，命下，乃得河東；

translations.literal: Because his father was old he begged an outside post and was appointed to supervise Huaidong educational affairs for convenient support of his parents; when the order came down he had received Hedong instead;
translations.idiomatic: Because his father was elderly he asked for an outside post and was appointed to supervise educational affairs in Huaidong so he could care for his parents at home. When the appointment was issued, he had been given Hedong instead;

sentences.zh: 而為淮東者，臧祐之也。

translations.literal: and the one who received Huaidong was Zang Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: the man who received Huaidong was Zang Youzhi.

sentences.zh: 蓋省吏取祐之賂，輒易之。

translations.literal: This was because a provincial clerk took bribes from Youzhi and simply exchanged the appointments.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk in the Secretariat had taken a bribe from Youzhi and simply swapped the two appointments.

sentences.zh: 或教使自言，熙靖曰：「事君不擇地，吾其可發人之私，求自便也？」

translations.literal: Someone urged him to report it himself. Xijing said: "In serving one's lord one does not choose the place; how could I expose another's private affair to seek my own convenience?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged him to report the matter himself. Xijing said, "In serving one's lord one does not choose the place—how could I expose another man's private wrongdoing for my own convenience?"

sentences.zh: 宰相聞而賢之，留為兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: The chief minister heard and considered him worthy; he was retained as vice director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister heard of this and admired him; Xijing was kept at court as vice director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂去，還，為右司員外郎。

translations.literal: He left on his father's mourning, returned, and became vice director of the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father, then returned as vice director of the Right Office.

sentences.zh: 王黼乙太宰領應奉司，又方事燕雲，立經撫房於中書獨專之，他執政皆不得預。

translations.literal: Wang Fu, having resigned as Grand Chancellor, still headed the Imperial Offerings Office; he was also then engaged in Yan-Yun affairs and established a frontier pacification office within the Secretariat that he alone controlled; other chief ministers could not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu had stepped down as Grand Chancellor but still headed the Imperial Offerings Office. He was then pursuing the Yan-Yun campaign and set up a frontier pacification office within the Secretariat that he alone controlled; the other chief ministers were excluded.

sentences.zh: 熙靖與言曰：「應奉之職，非宰相所當預。

translations.literal: Xijing spoke to him and said: "The duties of imperial offerings are not what a chief minister should undertake.
translations.idiomatic: Xijing told him, "The duties of the Imperial Offerings Office are not what a chief minister should take on.

sentences.zh: 尚書、樞密皆有兵房，足以治疆事，經撫何為者哉？」

translations.literal: The Ministry and the Bureau of Military Affairs each have military offices sufficient to manage frontier affairs—what is a frontier pacification office for?"
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry and the Bureau of Military Affairs each have military sections fully able to handle frontier affairs—what need is there for a separate pacification office?"

sentences.zh: 黼積不樂。

translations.literal: Fu grew increasingly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Fu grew steadily more displeased with him.

sentences.zh: 同列五人皆躐躋禁從，獨滯留四年。

translations.literal: Five colleagues all leaped into palace attendance; he alone was held back four years.
translations.idiomatic: Five colleagues all vaulted into palace attendance posts while he alone was held back for four years.

sentences.zh: 都水丞失職，移過於熙靖，貶其兩秩，又將左轉為國子司業，執政交言不可，僅遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: The director of waterways lost his post and shifted the blame onto Xijing; Xijing was demoted two ranks and was about to be transferred left to director of the National University; the chief ministers all said this could not be done, and he was only moved to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the director of waterways lost his post he shifted the blame to Xijing, who was demoted two ranks and slated for transfer to director of the National University. The chief ministers protested that this was unacceptable, and he was moved only to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 黼罷，乃拜中書舍人，蔡攸又惡之，出知拱州。

translations.literal: When Fu was dismissed Xijing was appointed Secretariat drafter; Cai You again hated him and he was sent out as prefect of Gongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu fell from power Xijing was made a Secretariat drafter, but Cai You also disliked him and he was sent out as prefect of Gongzhou.

sentences.zh: 越兩月，復以故官召，入對言：「燕山雖定，宜益謹思患豫防之戒。」

translations.literal: After two months he was again summoned to his former office; entering audience he said: "Though Yan Mountain is settled, we should all the more heed the warning to think of trouble beforehand and take preventive care."
translations.idiomatic: Two months later he was recalled to his former post. At audience he said, "Though Yan Mountain is settled, we should be all the more careful to heed the warning to think of trouble before it comes and take preventive measures."

sentences.zh: 徽宗曰：「《詩》所謂'迨天之未陰雨，徹彼桑土，綢繆牖戶'者是也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong said: "It is what the Odes call, 'Before heaven has not yet darkened with rain, gather that mulberry bark and bind up the window and door.'"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong said, "That is what the Odes mean: 'Before the sky has darkened with rain, gather mulberry bark and bind up the windows and doors.'"

sentences.zh: 熙靖進曰：「孔子云：'為此詩者，其知道乎！

translations.literal: Xijing advanced and said: "Confucius said, 'The maker of this ode—did he know the Way!
translations.idiomatic: Xijing went on, "Confucius said of that ode, 'Its author knew the Way!

sentences.zh: 能治其國家，誰敢侮之？

translations.literal: He who can govern his state well—who would dare insult him?
translations.idiomatic: He who can govern his state well—who would dare insult him?

sentences.zh: '願陛下為無疆之計。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to plan for boundless security."
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will plan for lasting security.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，同譚世勣事龍德宮，改顯謨閣待制、提舉醴泉觀。

translations.literal: Early in Jingkang he served the Longde Palace together with Tan Shiji, was changed to Xianmo Hall attendant, and supervised the Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingkang era he served at Longde Palace together with Tan Shiji, was made attendant of the Xianmo Hall, and put in charge of the Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 道君待之甚厚，常從容及內禪事，曰：「外人以為吳敏功，殊不知此自出吾意耳，吾苟不欲，人言且滅族，誰敢哉？

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor treated him very generously and often spoke at ease of the inner abdication, saying: "Outsiders think Wu Min accomplished it, but they do not know this came from my own intent. If I had not wished it, talk would have brought extermination of the clan—who would have dared?
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor treated him with great favor and often spoke calmly of his abdication, saying, "Outsiders credit Wu Min, but they do not know this came from my own wish. If I had not wanted it, rumor would have destroyed my whole clan—who would have dared oppose me?

sentences.zh: 或謂吾似唐睿宗上畏天戒，故為之，吾有此心久矣。」

translations.literal: Some say I resemble Tang Ruizong in fearing heaven's warning and therefore did it—I have had this heart long ago."
translations.idiomatic: Some say I resemble Tang Ruizong, who abdicated in awe of heaven's warning—but I have had this intention for a long time."

sentences.zh: 熙靖再拜賀。

translations.literal: Xijing bowed twice in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Xijing bowed twice in congratulation.

sentences.zh: 敏聞而忌之，以進對不時受罰。

translations.literal: Min heard and resented this; for untimely audience he was punished.
translations.idiomatic: When Min heard of this he grew jealous and had Xijing punished for presenting himself at audience at an improper time.

sentences.zh: 既拒張邦昌之命，憂憤廢食，家人進粥藥寬譬之，終無生意。

translations.literal: After he refused Zhang Bangchang's order he grieved and raged and abandoned food; his family brought porridge and medicine to comfort him, but in the end he had no will to live.
translations.idiomatic: After he refused Zhang Bangchang's summons he was consumed by grief and anger and would not eat. His family brought porridge and medicine to comfort him, but he had no will to live.

sentences.zh: 故人視其病，相持啜泣，索筆書唐王維所賦「百官何日再朝天」之句，明日遂卒，年五十三，與世勣同贈端明殿學士。

translations.literal: An old friend visited his illness; they held each other weeping. He asked for a brush and wrote the line Tang Wang Wei composed, "When will the hundred officials again attend court at dawn?" The next day he died at age fifty-three; together with Shiji he was posthumously granted academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: An old friend came to see him in his illness; they embraced and wept. He asked for a brush and wrote Wang Wei's line, "When will the hundred officials again bow at dawn court?" He died the next day at fifty-three; he and Shiji were both posthumously made academicians of the Duanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 王雲，字子飛，澤州人。

translations.literal: Wang Yun, styled Zifei, was a man of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun, courtesy name Zifei, was a native of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 父獻可，仕至英州刺史、知瀘州。

translations.literal: His father Xiankhe served to Yingzhou prefect and Luzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiankhe rose to prefect of Yingzhou and administrator of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 黃庭堅謫於涪，獻可遇之甚厚，時人稱之。

translations.literal: Huang Tingjian was exiled to Fu; Xiankhe treated him very generously, and men of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Tingjian was exiled to Fu, Xiankhe treated him with great kindness, and contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 雲舉進士，從使高麗，撰《雞林志》以進。

translations.literal: Yun passed the jinshi examination, followed an embassy to Goryeo, and composed the Record of Goguryeo to present.
translations.idiomatic: Yun passed the jinshi examination, accompanied an embassy to Goryeo, and composed the Record of Goguryeo, which he presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 擢秘書省校書郎，出知簡州，遷陝西轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to collator of the Secretariat, sent out as Jianzhou prefect, and transferred to Shaanxi transport vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to collator in the Secretariat, served as prefect of Jianzhou, and was transferred to vice transport commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 宣和中，從童貫宣撫幕，入為兵部員外郎、起居中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the Xuanhe era he followed Tong Guan's pacification staff, entered court as vice director of the Ministry of War and Secretariat drafter for imperial audiences.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuanhe era he served on Tong Guan's pacification staff, then entered court as vice director of the Ministry of War and Secretariat drafter for imperial audiences.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，以給事中使斡離不軍，議割三鎮以和。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang he was sent as supervising secretary to Wanyan Zonghan's army to negotiate ceding the three prefectures for peace.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang 1 he was sent as supervising secretary to Wanyan Zonghan's camp to negotiate ceding the three prefectures in exchange for peace.

sentences.zh: 使還，傳道斡離不之意，以為黏罕得朝廷所與餘睹蠟書，堅雲中國不可信，欲敗和約。

translations.literal: On his return he relayed Zonghan's meaning, saying that Wanyan Aguda had obtained from the court a wax-sealed letter to Yelü Yu, and firmly declared China untrustworthy, wishing to break the peace treaty.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported Zonghan's message: Aguda had obtained a wax-sealed letter from the court to Yelü Yu and insisted that the Song could not be trusted, intending to break the peace treaty.

sentences.zh: 執政以為不然，罷為徽猷閣待制、知唐州。

translations.literal: The chief ministers did not believe this and dismissed him to Xianyou Hall attendant and Tangzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers disagreed and demoted him to attendant of the Xianyou Hall and prefect of Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 金人陷太原，召拜刑部尚書，再出使，許以三鎮賦入之數。

translations.literal: When the Jin took Taiyuan he was summoned as Minister of Justice and sent out again, offering the tax revenue of the three prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin captured Taiyuan he was recalled as Minister of Justice and sent on another embassy, offering the tax revenue of the three prefectures.

sentences.zh: 雲至真定，遣從吏李裕還言：「金人不復求地，但索五輅及上尊號，且須康王來，和好乃成。」

translations.literal: Yun reached Zhending and sent his attendant Li Yu back with word: "The Jin no longer seek territory but demand the five imperial carriages and an exalted title, and moreover require the Prince of Kang to come before peace can be concluded."
translations.idiomatic: Yun reached Zhending and sent his attendant Li Yu back with word that the Jin no longer demanded territory but wanted the five imperial carriages and an exalted title for the emperor, and that the Prince of Kang must come before peace could be made.

sentences.zh: 欽宗悉從之，且命王及馮澥往。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong followed all of this and also ordered Wang and Feng Xie to go.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong agreed to everything and ordered Wang and Feng Xie to go as well.

sentences.zh: 未行，而車輅至長垣，為所卻，雲亦還。

translations.literal: Before they departed the imperial carriages reached Changyuan and were turned back; Yun also returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could set out the imperial carriages reached Changyuan and were turned back, and Yun returned as well.

sentences.zh: 澥奏言雲誕妄誤國，雲言：「事勢中變，金人必欲得三鎮，不然，則進兵取汴都。」

translations.literal: Feng memorialized that Yun's fabrications had harmed the state. Yun said: "The situation has changed midway; the Jin will certainly want the three prefectures, or else they will advance to take Bian capital."
translations.idiomatic: Feng memorialized that Yun's fabrications had harmed the state. Yun said, "The situation has changed—the Jin will certainly demand the three prefectures, or they will advance on the capital at Bian."

sentences.zh: 中外震駭，詔集百官議，雲固言：「康王舊與斡離不結歡，宜將命。」

translations.literal: Court and country were shaken; an edict gathered all officials to deliberate. Yun firmly said: "The Prince of Kang once formed friendly ties with Zonghan and should carry the mission."
translations.idiomatic: Court and country were shaken. An edict summoned all officials to deliberate. Yun insisted, "The Prince of Kang once won Zonghan's favor and should carry the mission."

sentences.zh: 帝慮為所留，雲曰：「和議既成，必無留王之理，臣敢以百口保之。」

translations.literal: The emperor feared he would be detained. Yun said: "Once peace is concluded there can be no reason to detain the prince; I dare guarantee this with the lives of a hundred in my household."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared the prince would be detained. Yun said, "Once peace is made there will be no grounds to hold him—I stake the lives of my entire household on it."

sentences.zh: 王遂受命，而雲以資政殿學士為之副。

translations.literal: The prince then received the commission, and Yun served as his deputy as academician of the Zizheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The prince accepted the commission, with Yun as his deputy in the rank of academician of the Zizheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 頃雲奉使過磁、相，勸兩郡徹近城民舍，運粟入保，為清野之計，民怨之。

translations.literal: Earlier when Yun went on embassy he passed Ci and Xiang, urging both prefectures to clear dwellings near the cities, transport grain into the forts, and adopt a scorched-earth plan; the people resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on embassy, Yun had passed through Ci and Xiang and urged both prefectures to clear dwellings near the cities, move grain into the forts, and adopt a scorched-earth strategy—the people resented him for it.

sentences.zh: 及是，次磁州，又與守臣宗澤有憾。

translations.literal: On this occasion he halted at Cizhou and again had a grudge against the defending official Zong Ze.
translations.idiomatic: On this journey he halted at Cizhou and again bore a grudge against the defending official Zong Ze.

sentences.zh: 於是王出謁嘉應神祠，雲在後，民遮道諫曰：「肅王已為金人所留，王不宜北去。」

translations.literal: Then the prince went out to pay respects at the Jiaying Spirit Shrine with Yun behind; the people blocked the road and remonstrated: "Prince Su was already detained by the Jin; Your Highness should not go north."
translations.idiomatic: The prince went out to pay respects at the Jiaying Spirit Shrine with Yun behind him. The people blocked the road and pleaded, "Prince Su was already detained by the Jin—Your Highness must not go north."

sentences.zh: 厲聲指雲曰：「清野之人，真奸賊也。」

translations.literal: They pointed at Yun in a harsh voice and said: "The man of the scorched earth—he is a true traitor."
translations.idiomatic: They pointed at Yun and shouted, "The man who ordered the scorched earth—he is a true traitor!"

sentences.zh: 王出廟行，或發雲笥，得烏絁短巾，蓋雲夙有風眩疾，寢則以護首者。

translations.literal: The prince left the shrine and set out; someone opened Yun's trunk and found a black silk headcloth—Yun had long suffered from vertigo and used it to protect his head when sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: As the prince left the shrine someone opened Yun's trunk and found a black silk headcloth—Yun had long suffered from vertigo and wore it to protect his head when he slept.

sentences.zh: 民益信其為奸，噪而殺之。

translations.literal: The people believed all the more that he was a traitor, clamored, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd was convinced he was a traitor, raised a clamor, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 王見事勢洶洶，乃南還相州。

translations.literal: The prince, seeing the situation turbulent, turned south and returned to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the uproar, the prince turned south and returned to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是役也，雲不死，王必北行，議者以是驗天命雲。

translations.literal: In this affair, had Yun not died the prince would certainly have gone north; commentators took this as proof of Heaven's mandate through Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Had Yun not died on this mission, the prince would surely have gone north; commentators took his death as proof that Heaven had intervened through Yun.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，贈觀文殿學士。

translations.literal: Early in Jianyan he was posthumously granted academician of the Guanwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyan era he was posthumously made academician of the Guanwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 雲兄霽，崇甯時，為謀議司詳議官，上書告蔡京罪，黥隸海島。

translations.literal: Yun's elder brother Ji, in the Chongning era, was a detailed reviewer in the Policy Deliberation Office; he memorialized accusing Cai Jing of crimes and was tattooed and exiled to a sea island.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's elder brother Ji, during the Chongning era, served as a detailed reviewer in the Policy Deliberation Office. He memorialized accusing Cai Jing of crimes and was tattooed and exiled to a sea island.

sentences.zh: 欽宗復其官，從種師中戰死。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong restored his office; he followed Zhong Shizhong and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong restored his rank; he followed Zhong Shizhong and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 譚世勣

translations.literal: Tan Shiji
translations.idiomatic: Tan Shiji

sentences.zh: 譚世勣字彥成，潭州長沙人。

translations.literal: Tan Shiji, styled Yancheng, was a man of Changsha in Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Shiji, courtesy name Yancheng, was a native of Changsha in Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，教授郴州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was instructor at Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as instructor at Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 時王氏學盛行，世勣雅不喜。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Anshi's learning flourished; Shiji had never liked it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi's school was then in vogue, but Shiji had never cared for it.

sentences.zh: 或問之，曰：「說多而屢變，無不易之論也。」

translations.literal: When asked about it he said: "Too many doctrines and constant changes—there is no stable teaching."
translations.idiomatic: When asked about it he said, "Too many doctrines and too many changes—there is no teaching that does not shift."

sentences.zh: 置其書不觀。

translations.literal: He set their books aside and did not read them.
translations.idiomatic: He set their books aside and would not read them.

sentences.zh: 又中詞學兼茂科，除秘書省正字。

translations.literal: He also passed the erudite literary examination and was appointed collator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He also passed the erudite literary examination and was appointed collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時相蔡京子攸領書局，同舍郎多翕附以取貴仕。

translations.literal: The chief minister Cai Jing's son You headed the book bureau; many colleagues in the lodge fawned on him to win high office.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister's son Cai You headed the book bureau, and many colleagues curried favor with him to win high office.

sentences.zh: 世勣獨坐直廬，繙書竟日。

translations.literal: Shiji alone sat in the duty lodge turning pages of books all day.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji alone sat in the duty lodge reading books all day.

sentences.zh: 梁師成之客與為鄰居，數致師成願交意，謝不答。

translations.literal: A client of Liang Shicheng was his neighbor and several times conveyed Liang's wish for friendship; he declined to respond.
translations.idiomatic: A client of Liang Shicheng lived nearby and repeatedly conveyed Liang's wish for friendship; Shiji declined.

sentences.zh: 在館六年不遷，京罷，用久次為司門員外郎。

translations.literal: Six years in the lodge without promotion; when Jing fell he was appointed vice director of the Gate Office by seniority.
translations.idiomatic: After six years in the lodge without promotion, when Cai Jing fell he was appointed vice director of the Gate Office by seniority.

sentences.zh: 又三年，遷吏部。

translations.literal: Three years later he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 京復相，嫌不附己，罷提點太平宮。

translations.literal: When Jing returned as chief minister he resented that Shiji did not attach himself to him and dismissed him to supervise the Taiping Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing returned to power he resented Shiji's independence and dismissed him to supervise the Taiping Palace.

sentences.zh: 久之，復還吏部。

translations.literal: After a long while he returned to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was restored to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 幸臣妄引恩澤任子，持不與。

translations.literal: A favored minister falsely invoked grace to appoint his son; Shiji held firm and would not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: A favored minister tried to use imperial favor to appoint his son; Shiji refused.

sentences.zh: 吏白有某例，世勣曰：「豈當以暫例破成法！」

translations.literal: The clerk reported there was a certain precedent. Shiji said: "How can a temporary precedent break established law!"
translations.idiomatic: A clerk cited a precedent. Shiji said, "How can a temporary precedent overturn established law!"

sentences.zh: 已而取中旨行之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they took an inner edict and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they obtained an inner edict and carried it out anyway.

sentences.zh: 進少府監，擢中書舍人，以謹命令、惜名器、廣言路、吝賜予、正上供、省浮費六事言於上，又為當路所嫉。

translations.literal: Promoted to director of the Palace Workshops, he was elevated to Secretariat drafter and addressed the throne on six matters: strict orders, cherishing titles, broadening the avenue of remonstrance, sparing grants, correcting tribute, and reducing waste—and again was envied by those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to director of the Palace Workshops and then to Secretariat drafter, he addressed the throne on six matters—strict enforcement of orders, respect for official titles, a broader avenue of remonstrance, restraint in grants, correction of tribute, and reduction of waste—and again earned the jealousy of those in power.

sentences.zh: 以徽猷閣待制知婺州，未行，復留之。

translations.literal: He was made Xianyou Hall attendant and Wuzhou prefect but before departing was kept back.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attendant of the Xianyou Hall and prefect of Wuzhou, but before he could leave he was kept at court.

sentences.zh: 徽宗禪位東幸，且還，使與李熙靖副執政奉迎，遂同主管龍德宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong abdicated and traveled east and then returned, he and Li Xijing were made deputies to the chief ministers to welcome him, and together supervised Longde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong abdicated, traveled east, and then returned, Shiji and Li Xijing were made deputies to the chief ministers to welcome him and together took charge of Longde Palace.

sentences.zh: 請辨正宣仁國史之謗，述欽聖遺旨以復瑤華，大享神祖仍用富弼侑食，釋奠先聖不當以王安石配，後皆施行。

translations.literal: He asked to correct the slander in the national history concerning Empress Xuanren, set forth Empress Qinsheng's testament to restore Yaohua, that great sacrifices to Shenzong should still use Fu Bi as companion in the offering, and that sacrifices to the Sage should not pair Wang Anshi—all were later carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to correct the slanders in the national history concerning Empress Xuanren, cited Empress Qinsheng's testament to restore Yaohua, argued that great sacrifices to Shenzong should still use Fu Bi as companion spirit, and that Wang Anshi should not share the sage's altar—all were later adopted.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，彗出東方，大臣或謂此四夷將衰之兆，世勣面奏：「垂象可畏，當修德以應天，不宜惑諛說。」

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn a comet appeared in the east; some ministers said this was a sign the four barbarians would decline. Shiji addressed the throne in person: "Heaven's signs are to be feared; we should cultivate virtue to respond to Heaven and not be misled by flattery."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month a comet appeared in the east. Some ministers said it foretold the decline of the barbarians. Shiji addressed the throne: "Heaven's signs are alarming—we should cultivate virtue to answer Heaven, not be misled by flattery."

sentences.zh: 進給事中兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary and concurrent reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary and concurrent reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 內侍喧爭殿門，詔以贖論，世勣駁其不恭，因言：「童貫輩初亦甚微，小惡不懲，將馴至大患。」

translations.literal: Inner attendants clamored and quarreled at the palace gate; an edict treated it with ransom discussion. Shiji rebutted their lack of respect and said: "Tong Guan and his kind were at first very minor; if small wrongs are not punished they will grow into great calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants quarreled loudly at the palace gate; an edict proposed handling the matter with fines. Shiji objected to their disrespect and said, "Men like Tong Guan were once insignificant too—if small offenses go unpunished, great disasters will follow."

sentences.zh: 疏入，同類側目。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, his peers glared sideways.
translations.idiomatic: When his memorial was submitted, his peers glared at him.

sentences.zh: 何栗建議分外郡為四道，置都總管，事得顓決。

translations.literal: He Li proposed dividing outer prefectures into four circuits, establishing overall commanders with sole decision in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He Li proposed dividing the outer prefectures into four circuits, each with an overall commander empowered to decide affairs on his own.

sentences.zh: 世勣言：「裂天下以付四人，而王畿所治者才十六縣，獨無尾大不掉之慮乎？」

translations.literal: Shiji said: "To split the realm among four men while the imperial domain governs only sixteen counties—have we no fear of a tail too large to wag?"
translations.idiomatic: Shiji said, "To split the realm among four men while the capital district governs only sixteen counties—do we not fear a tail too heavy to control?"

sentences.zh: 栗不樂。

translations.literal: Li was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He Li was displeased.

sentences.zh: 改禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shiji was changed to vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 金騎駸駸南下，世勣言：「守邊為上策；

translations.literal: Jin cavalry pressed south in droves. Shiji said: "Holding the frontier is the best strategy;
translations.idiomatic: As Jin cavalry pressed south in waves, Shiji said, "Holding the frontier is the best strategy;

sentences.zh: 今邊不得守，守河則京畿自固，中策也；

translations.literal: now that the frontier cannot be held, holding the river will make the capital region secure by itself—the middle strategy;
translations.idiomatic: now that the frontier cannot be held, holding the Yellow River will secure the capital region—the middle strategy;

sentences.zh: 巡幸江、淮，會東南兵以捍敵，下策也。

translations.literal: touring the Yangzi and Huai, gathering southeast troops to resist the enemy—the worst strategy.
translations.idiomatic: touring the Yangzi and Huai and gathering southeast troops to resist the enemy—the worst strategy.

sentences.zh: 金人既渡河，又請遣大將秦元以所部京畿保甲，分護國門，使兵勢連屬，首尾相援，即金人不敢逼。

translations.literal: Once the Jin had crossed the river he again asked to send the great general Qin Yuan with his capital-region militia to guard the city gates in sections so that military strength would link up and head and tail support each other—then the Jin would not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin crossed the river he again asked that the general Qin Yuan be sent with his capital-region militia to guard the city gates in sections so forces could link up from end to end—then the Jin would not dare press the city.

sentences.zh: 孫傅深然之，又格于栗議。

translations.literal: Sun Fu deeply approved, but it was blocked by He's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu strongly agreed, but the plan was blocked by He Li's opposition.

sentences.zh: 再扈車駕至金帥帳，以十害說其用事者，言講解之利，詞意忠激，金人聳聽。

translations.literal: He again accompanied the imperial carriage to the Jin commander's tent, used ten harms to persuade those in power, spoke of the benefits of negotiation, his words loyal and impassioned; the Jin listened with raised attention.
translations.idiomatic: He again accompanied the imperial carriage to the Jin commander's tent, laid out ten harms to persuade their leaders, and argued the benefits of negotiation with loyal, impassioned words that made the Jin listen intently.

sentences.zh: 張邦昌僭國，令與李熙靖同直學士院，皆稱疾臥不起，以憂卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: When Zhang Bangchang usurped the state he ordered Shiji and Li Xijing to serve together in the Hanlin Academy; both claimed illness and would not rise, and died of grief at age fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Bangchang usurped the throne he ordered Shiji and Li Xijing to serve together in the Hanlin Academy. Both claimed illness and refused to rise; Shiji died of grief at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，褒其守節，贈端明殿學士。

translations.literal: Early in Jianyan his steadfast integrity was praised and he was posthumously granted academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyan era his steadfast integrity was praised and he was posthumously made academician of the Duanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 梅執禮

translations.literal: Mei Zhili
translations.idiomatic: Mei Zhili

sentences.zh: 梅執禮，字和勝，婺州浦江人。

translations.literal: Mei Zhili, styled Hesheng, was a man of Pujiang in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Zhili, courtesy name Hesheng, was a native of Pujiang in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調常山尉未赴，以薦為敕令刪定官、武學博士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as Changshan assistant magistrate but did not take up the post, and by recommendation became an editor of imperial commands and doctor of the Military Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as assistant magistrate of Changshan but did not take up the post. By recommendation he became an editor of imperial commands and doctor of the Military Academy.

sentences.zh: 大司成強淵明賢其人，為宰相言，相以未嘗識面為慊。

translations.literal: The grand director Qiang Yuanming considered him worthy and spoke of him to the chief minister; the minister regretted that he had never met him in person.
translations.idiomatic: The grand director Qiang Yuanming admired him and spoke of him to the chief minister, who regretted that he had never met him.

sentences.zh: 執禮聞之曰：「以人言而得，必以人言而失，吾求在我者而已。」

translations.literal: Zhili heard and said: "What is gained through others' words will be lost through others' words; I seek only what depends on myself."
translations.idiomatic: Zhili heard this and said, "What is gained through others' words can be lost through others' words—I rely only on what is in myself."

sentences.zh: 卒不往謁。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go to pay a visit.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he never went to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 曆軍器、鴻臚丞，比部員外郎，比部職勾稽財貨，文牘山委，率不暇經目。

translations.literal: He served as director in the Armory and Honglu, then vice director in the Revenue Section; the Revenue Section's duty was to audit goods and funds, documents piled like mountains, and he generally had no time to read them all.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Armory and Honglu bureaus, then as vice director of the Revenue Section, whose duty was to audit goods and funds. Documents piled up like mountains and he generally had no time to read them all.

sentences.zh: 苑吏有持茶券至為錢三百萬者，以楊戩旨意迫取甚急。

translations.literal: A park clerk presented a tea certificate worth three million in cash and, on Yang Kai's order, pressed for collection with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: A park clerk presented a tea certificate worth three million cash and, on Yang Kai's orders, pressed for payment with great urgency.

sentences.zh: 執禮一閱，知其妄，欲白之，長貳疑不敢，乃獨列上，界詐也。

translations.literal: Zhili read it once and knew it was false; he wished to report it but his superiors hesitated and dared not; he alone memorialized that it was a border fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili read it once and saw it was fraudulent. His superiors hesitated to report it, so he memorialized alone that it was a false claim.

sentences.zh: 改度支、吏部，進國子司業兼資善堂翊善，遷左司員外郎，擢中書舍人、給事中。

translations.literal: Transferred to Revenue and Personnel, promoted to vice director of the National University and concurrent tutor of the Zishan Hall, moved to vice director of the Left Office, elevated to Secretariat drafter and supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Revenue and Personnel, promoted to vice director of the National University and concurrent tutor of the Zishan Hall, moved to vice director of the Left Office, and elevated to Secretariat drafter and supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 林攄以前執政赴闕宿留，冀復故職，執禮論去之。

translations.literal: Lin Shu, a former chief minister, came to court and lingered, hoping to recover his old office; Zhili argued for his removal.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Shu, a former chief minister, came to court and lingered, hoping to recover his old post; Zhili argued for his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 孟昌齡居鄆質人屋，當贖不肯與，而請中旨奪之，外郡卒留役中都者萬數，肆不逞為奸，詔悉令還，楊戩占不遣；

translations.literal: Meng Changling lived in a house in Yun pledged to a creditor and, when it should have been redeemed, refused to yield it and asked an inner edict to seize it; tens of thousands of soldiers from outer prefectures left on service in the capital ran riot and committed outrages—an edict ordered them all returned but Yang Kai held them back and would not release them;
translations.idiomatic: Meng Changling occupied a house in Yun pledged to a creditor and, when it should have been redeemed, refused to yield it and sought an inner edict to seize it. Tens of thousands of soldiers from outer prefectures left on service in the capital ran riot—an edict ordered them all sent home, but Yang Kai held them back;

sentences.zh: 內侍張佑董葺太廟，僭求賞：皆駁奏弗行。

translations.literal: the inner attendant Zhang You supervised repairs to the Imperial Ancestral Temple and presumptuously sought reward—all were rebutted in memorial and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: the inner attendant Zhang You supervised repairs to the Imperial Ancestral Temple and presumptuously sought a reward—Zhili memorialized against each request and none was granted.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 素與王黼善，黼嘗置酒其第，誇示園池妓妾之盛，有驕色。

translations.literal: He had long been friendly with Wang Fu; Fu once gave a banquet at his residence and displayed the splendor of gardens, ponds, and courtesans with a proud air.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been on good terms with Wang Fu, who once gave a banquet at Zhili's residence and displayed the splendor of his gardens, ponds, and courtesans with evident pride.

sentences.zh: 執禮曰：「公為宰相，當與天下同憂樂。

translations.literal: Zhili said: "As chief minister you should share the realm's joys and sorrows.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili said, "As chief minister you should share the realm's joys and sorrows.

sentences.zh: 今方臘流毒吳地，瘡痍未息，是豈歌舞宴樂時乎？」

translations.literal: Now Fang La's poison flows through Wu lands and the wounds have not healed—is this a time for song, dance, and feasting?"
translations.idiomatic: Fang La's poison still ravages Wu, and the wounds have not healed—is this a time for song, dance, and feasting?"

sentences.zh: 退又戒之以詩。

translations.literal: On leaving he again admonished him with a poem.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving he admonished him again in verse.

sentences.zh: 黼愧怒，會孟饗原廟後至，以顯謨閣待制知蘄州，又奪職。

translations.literal: Fu was ashamed and angry; when Zhili arrived late after the Meng sacrifice at the original temple he was made Xianmo Hall attendant and Qizhou prefect, and then stripped of office again.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was shamed and angry. When Zhili arrived late after the Meng sacrifice at the original temple he was demoted to attendant of the Xianmo Hall and prefect of Qizhou, then stripped of office again.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙滁州，復集英殿修撰。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Chuzhou and restored as compiler of the Jiying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to Chuzhou and restored as compiler of the Jiying Hall.

sentences.zh: 時賦鹽虧額，滁亦苦抑配。

translations.literal: At the time the salt tax fell short of quota and Chuzhou also suffered forced allotment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the salt tax fell short of its quota, and Chuzhou also suffered from forced allotment.

sentences.zh: 執禮曰：「郡不能當蘇、杭一邑，而食鹽乃倍粟數，民何以堪？」

translations.literal: Zhili said: "The prefecture cannot equal one district of Su or Hang, yet salt consumption doubles the grain quota—how can the people bear it?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhili said, "This prefecture cannot equal a single district of Suzhou or Hangzhou, yet the salt levy doubles the grain quota—how can the people bear it?"

sentences.zh: 請於朝，詔損二十萬，滁人德之。

translations.literal: He petitioned the court; an edict reduced it by two hundred thousand and the people of Chu were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned the court; an edict reduced the levy by two hundred thousand, and the people of Chuzhou were grateful.

sentences.zh: 欽宗立，徙知鎮江府，召為翰林學士，道除吏部尚書，旋改戶部。

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong ascended he was transferred to Zhenjiang prefecture, summoned as Hanlin academician, en route appointed Minister of Personnel, then soon changed to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Qinzong ascended the throne he was transferred to Zhenjiang, summoned as Hanlin academician, appointed Minister of Personnel en route, then soon transferred to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 方軍興，調度不足，執禮請以禁內錢隸有司，凡六宮廩給，皆由度支乃得下。

translations.literal: With war beginning, funds were insufficient; Zhili asked that palace funds be placed under the regular offices so that all provisions for the six palaces would pass through Revenue before release.
translations.idiomatic: With war under way, funds ran short. Zhili asked that palace funds be placed under the regular offices so that all provisions for the six palaces would pass through the Revenue Bureau before release.

sentences.zh: 嘗有小黃門持中批詣部取錢，而封識不用璽，既悟其失，復取之。

translations.literal: Once a minor yellow-gate attendant came to the ministry with an inner draft to withdraw money, but the seal did not use the imperial seal; realizing the error, he took it back.
translations.idiomatic: Once a minor palace attendant came to the ministry with an inner draft to withdraw money, but the seal did not bear the imperial seal. Realizing the error, he took the draft back.

sentences.zh: 執禮奏審，詔責典寶夫人而杖黃門。

translations.literal: Zhili memorialized for investigation; an edict rebuked the keeper of the seals and caned the yellow-gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili memorialized for investigation; an edict rebuked the keeper of the seals and had the attendant beaten.

sentences.zh: 金人圍京都，執禮勸帝親征，而請太上帝后、皇后、太子皆出避，用事者沮之。

translations.literal: When the Jin besieged the capital Zhili urged the emperor to campaign in person and asked that the Retired Emperor, empress, and crown prince all withdraw to safety; those in power obstructed this.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin besieged the capital Zhili urged the emperor to take the field in person and asked that the Retired Emperor, the empress, and the crown prince all withdraw to safety—those in power blocked the plan.

sentences.zh: 洎失守，金人質天子，邀金帛以數百千萬計，曰：「和議已定，但所需滿數，則奉天子還闕。」

translations.literal: When the city fell the Jin held the emperor hostage and demanded gold and silk in the tens of millions, saying: "Peace is already settled; once what is required reaches the full amount we will return the Son of Heaven to the palace."
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell the Jin held the emperor hostage and demanded gold and silk in the tens of millions, saying, "Peace is already settled—once the full sum is paid we will return the Son of Heaven to the palace."

sentences.zh: 執禮與同列陳知質、程振、安扶皆主根索，四人哀民力已困，相與謀曰：「金人所欲無藝極，雖銅鐵亦不能給，盍以軍法結罪，儻窒其求。」

translations.literal: Zhili and his colleagues Chen Zhizhi, Cheng Zhen, and An Fu all headed the search for funds. The four men grieved that the people's strength was exhausted and plotted together: "What the Jin desire has no limit; even copper and iron could not satisfy them—why not fix guilt under military law and perhaps block their demands?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhili and his colleagues Chen Zhizhi, Cheng Zhen, and An Fu all headed the search for funds. Grieving that the people were exhausted, the four plotted together: "The Jin demands are boundless—even copper and iron could not satisfy them. Why not fix guilt under military law and perhaps block their demands?"

sentences.zh: 而宦者挾宿怨語金帥曰：「城中七百萬戶，所取未百一，但許民持金銀換粟麥，當有出者。」

translations.literal: But eunuchs bearing old grudges told the Jin commander: "Within the city are seven million households; what has been taken is not one in a hundred—only allow the people to exchange gold and silver for grain and wheat and there will be those who come forward."
translations.idiomatic: But eunuchs bearing old grudges told the Jin commander, "The city holds seven million households—you have taken less than one in a hundred. Allow the people to exchange gold and silver for grain and wheat and they will come forward."

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: Before long it proved so.
translations.idiomatic: Before long it proved true.

sentences.zh: 酋怒，呼四人責之，對曰：「天子蒙塵，臣民皆願致死，雖肝腦不計，于金繒何有哉？

translations.literal: The chieftain was angry and summoned the four to rebuke them. They replied: "The Son of Heaven suffers in the dust; ministers and people all wish to die for him—even liver and brain are not counted; what of gold and silk?
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain was furious and summoned the four to rebuke them. They replied, "The Son of Heaven suffers in the dust—ministers and people alike would die for him without counting liver or brain; what of gold and silk?

sentences.zh: 顧比屋枵空，亡以塞命耳。」

translations.literal: Only every household is hollow and empty—there is nothing with which to fulfill the command."
translations.idiomatic: Only every household is hollow and empty—there is nothing with which to fulfill your command."

sentences.zh: 酋問官長何在，振恐執禮獲罪，遂前曰：「皆官長也。」

translations.literal: The chieftain asked where the chief officials were. Zhen feared Zhili would be punished and stepped forward: "We are all chief officials."
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain asked where the chief officials were. Zhen, fearing Zhili would bear the blame alone, stepped forward and said, "We are all chief officials."

sentences.zh: 酋益怒，先取其副胡舜陟、胡唐老、姚舜明、王俁，各杖之百。

translations.literal: The chieftain grew angrier still and first took his deputies Hu Shunzhi, Hu Tanglao, Yao Shunming, and Wang Hou, each caning them a hundred times.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain grew still angrier and first seized his deputies Hu Shunzhi, Hu Tanglao, Yao Shunming, and Wang Hou, caning each a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 執禮等猶為之請，俄遣還，將及門，呼下馬撾殺之，而梟其首，時靖康二年二月也。

translations.literal: Zhili and the others still pleaded for them. Soon they were sent back; as they neared the gate they were called down from their horses, clubbed to death, and their heads displayed—it was the second month of Jingkang 2.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili and the others still pleaded for them. They were soon sent back, but as they neared the gate they were called down from their horses, beaten to death, and their heads displayed—it was the second month of Jingkang 2.

sentences.zh: 是日，天宇晝冥，士庶皆隕涕憤歎。

translations.literal: That day the sky was dark at noon; scholars and commoners all shed tears in grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: That day the sky darkened at noon; scholars and commoners alike wept in grief and outrage.

sentences.zh: 初，車駕再出，執禮與宗室子昉、諸將吳革等謀集兵奪萬勝門，夜搗金帥帳，迎二帝以歸。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the imperial carriage went out again, Zhili with the imperial clansman Zifang and the generals Wu Ge and others plotted to gather troops, seize the Wansheng Gate, raid the Jin commander's tent by night, and welcome the two emperors back.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the imperial carriage went out again, Zhili joined the imperial clansman Zifang and the generals Wu Ge and others in a plot to gather troops, seize the Wansheng Gate, raid the Jin commander's tent by night, and bring the two emperors home.

sentences.zh: 而王時雍、徐秉哲使範瓊泄其謀，故不克。

translations.literal: But Wang Shiyong and Xu Bingzhe had Fan Qiong leak the plot, and so it failed.
translations.idiomatic: But Wang Shiyong and Xu Bingzhe had Fan Qiong betray the plot, and it failed.

sentences.zh: 死時，年四十九。

translations.literal: At his death he was forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-nine when he died.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，詔贈通奉大夫、端明殿學士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne an edict posthumously granted Senior Grandee of the Court for Imperial Offerings and academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, an edict posthumously granted Zhili the rank of Senior Grandee of the Court for Imperial Offerings and made him academician of the Duanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 議者以為薄，復加資政殿學士。

translations.literal: Critics thought this meager and he was further granted academician of the Zizheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Critics thought the reward too modest, and he was further made academician of the Zizheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 程振，字伯起，饒州樂平人。

translations.literal: Cheng Zhen, styled Boqi, was a man of Leping in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zhen, courtesy name Boqi, was a native of Leping in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 少有軼材，入太學，一時名輩多從之遊。

translations.literal: In youth he had outstanding talent; he entered the National University and many celebrated men of the time associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he showed outstanding talent. He entered the National University, and many celebrated men of the day sought his company.

sentences.zh: 徽宗幸學，以諸生右職除官，為辟雍錄，升博士，遷太常博士，提舉京東、西路學事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong visited the university he was appointed from among the students to a senior office, became Imperial Academy recorder, was promoted to erudite, transferred to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and supervised educational affairs in eastern and western Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong visited the university, Zhen was appointed from among the students to a senior post, became recorder of the Imperial Academy, was promoted to erudite, transferred to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and supervised educational affairs in eastern and western Jing.

sentences.zh: 請立廟于鄒祀孟軻，以公孫醜、萬章、樂正克等配食，從之。

translations.literal: He asked to establish a temple at Zou to sacrifice to Mencius, with Gongsun Chou, Wan Zhang, Yuezheng Ke, and others as companion spirits in the offering; the court agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to establish a temple at Zou to sacrifice to Mencius, with Gongsun Chou, Wan Zhang, Yuezheng Ke, and others as companion spirits at the altar, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 提舉京西常平，入為膳部員外郎、監察御史、辟雍國子司業、左司員外郎兼太子舍人。

translations.literal: He supervised western Jing Ever-Normal Granaries, entered court as vice director of the Provisions Bureau, investigating censor, Imperial Academy vice director of the National University, and vice director of the Left Office concurrent with crown prince attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the Ever-Normal Granaries of western Jing, then entered court as vice director of the Provisions Bureau, investigating censor, vice director of the National University at the Imperial Academy, and vice director of the Left Office concurrent with attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 始至，即言：「古者大祭禮登餕受爵，必以上嗣，既《禮經》所載，且元豐彝典具存。

translations.literal: As soon as he arrived he said: "In antiquity at the great sacrifice, when the offering was set out and wine received, it had to be the eldest heir—this is recorded in the Book of Rites, and the Yuanfeng canonical regulations still stand complete.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he took up his post he said, "In antiquity at the great sacrifice, when the offering was set out and wine received, it had to be the eldest heir—this is recorded in the Book of Rites, and the Yuanfeng canonical regulations still stand intact.

sentences.zh: 昨天子展事明堂，而殿下不預，非所以尊宗廟、重社稷也。」

translations.literal: Yesterday the Son of Heaven performed the rites at the Bright Hall while Your Highness did not participate—this is not how to honor the ancestral temple and esteem the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday the Son of Heaven performed the rites at the Bright Hall while Your Highness did not take part—this is not how to honor the ancestral temple and esteem the altars of soil and grain."

sentences.zh: 太子矍然曰：「宮僚初無及此者。」

translations.literal: The crown prince started and said: "Among the palace staff none had ever reached this point before."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince started and said, "None of my palace staff had ever raised this before."

sentences.zh: 由是特加獎異。

translations.literal: Because of this he was specially praised and favored.
translations.idiomatic: From this he won special praise and favor.

sentences.zh: 方臘起，振謂王黼宜乘此時建革天下弊事，以上當天意，下順人心。

translations.literal: When Fang La rose, Zhen told Wang Fu he should seize this moment to reform the world's abuses, matching Heaven above and winning hearts below.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang La rose, Zhen told Wang Fu he should seize the moment to reform the abuses of the realm, answering Heaven above and winning the people below.

sentences.zh: 黼不懌，曰：「上且疑黼挾寇，奈何？」

translations.literal: Fu was displeased and said: "His Majesty already suspects Fu of using the bandits—what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu was displeased and said, "His Majesty already suspects me of using the rebels for my own ends—what can I do?"

sentences.zh: 振知黼忌其言，趨而出，然太子薦之甚力，遂擢給事中。

translations.literal: Zhen knew Fu resented his words and hurried out, but the crown prince recommended him strongly and he was elevated to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen knew Fu resented his words and hurried out, but the crown prince strongly recommended him and he was elevated to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 黼白振資淺，且雅長書命，請以為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Fu told the court that Zhen's qualifications were shallow and that he excelled at drafting documents, asking that he be made Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Fu told the court that Zhen's qualifications were shallow and that he excelled at drafting documents, and asked that he be made a Secretariat drafter instead.

sentences.zh: 侍郎馮熙載出知亳州，黼怨熙載，欲振詆以醜語，振不肯。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Feng Xizai was sent out as Bozhou prefect; Fu resented Xizai and wanted Zhen to slander him with ugly words, but Zhen refused.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Feng Xizai was sent out as prefect of Bozhou. Fu resented him and wanted Zhen to slander him with ugly words, but Zhen refused.

sentences.zh: 黼使言者劾為黨，罷提舉沖佑觀。

translations.literal: Fu had critics impeach him as a factionalist and dismissed him to supervise the Chongyou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had critics impeach him as a factionalist, and he was dismissed to supervise the Chongyou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 居三年，復還故官。

translations.literal: After three years he returned to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，進吏部侍郎，為欽宗言：「柄臣不和，論議多駁，詔令輕改，失於事幾。

translations.literal: In Jingkang 1 he was promoted to vice minister of Personnel and told Emperor Qinzong: "The power-holders are not in harmony, deliberations are often rejected, edicts are lightly changed—opportunities are lost.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang 1 he was promoted to vice minister of Personnel and told Emperor Qinzong, "The power-holders are not in harmony, deliberations are constantly overturned, and edicts are lightly changed—opportunities are lost.

sentences.zh: 金人交兵半歲，而至今不解者，以和戰之說未一故也。

translations.literal: The Jin have been at war for half a year and it is still unresolved because the arguments for peace and war are not united.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin have been at war for half a year and the conflict remains unresolved because the court cannot agree on peace or war.

sentences.zh: 裁抑濫賞，如白黑易分，而數月之間，三變其議，以私心不除，各蔽其黨故也。

translations.literal: Restraining excessive rewards should be as easy as distinguishing black from white, yet within a few months the policy changed three times because private hearts were not removed and each sheltered his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Restraining excessive rewards should be as clear as black and white, yet within a few months the policy changed three times because private motives were not removed and each faction sheltered its own.

sentences.zh: 今日一人言之，以為是而行；

translations.literal: Today one man speaks and it is thought right and carried out;
translations.idiomatic: Today one man speaks and it is thought right and carried out;

sentences.zh: 明日一人言之，以為非而止。

translations.literal: tomorrow another speaks and it is thought wrong and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: tomorrow another speaks and it is thought wrong and stopped.

sentences.zh: 或聖斷隃度而不暇疇咨，或大臣偏見而遂形播告，所以動未必善，處未必宜，乃輒為之反汗，其勢不得不爾也。」

translations.literal: Sometimes the sacred decision is made in secret without time to consult broadly; sometimes a great minister's bias is broadcast as policy—thus actions are not necessarily good, measures not necessarily fitting, and edicts are repeatedly reversed; the situation must be so."
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes the emperor decides in secret without time for broad consultation; sometimes a minister's bias is broadcast as policy—so actions are not necessarily sound, measures not necessarily fitting, and edicts are repeatedly reversed. The situation cannot be otherwise."

sentences.zh: 時金兵至河北，振請糾諸道兵掎角擊之，曰：「彼猖獗如此，陛下尚欲守和議，而不使之少有懲艾乎？」
