translations.literal: At the time Jin troops reached Hebei; Zhen asked to gather troops from all circuits to strike from converging angles and said: "They are so rampant—does Your Majesty still wish to hold to peace and not let them suffer even a little correction?"
translations.idiomatic: When Jin troops reached Hebei, Zhen asked to gather troops from all circuits to strike them from converging angles. He said, "They are so rampant—does Your Majesty still wish to cling to peace and deny them even a little punishment?"

sentences.zh: 上嗟味其言，而牽於外廷，不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed over his words but was constrained by the outer court and could not use them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed over his words but was constrained by the outer court and could not act on them.

sentences.zh: 拜開封尹。

translations.literal: He was appointed Kaifeng prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 故時，大辟有情可矜，多奏取原貸；

translations.literal: In former times, for capital crimes where mercy was possible, many were memorialized for pardon;
translations.idiomatic: In former times, for capital crimes where mercy was possible, many were memorialized for pardon;

sentences.zh: 崇寧以來，議者謂輦轂先彈壓，率便文殺之。

translations.literal: since Chongning critics said the capital must be suppressed first and generally expedited execution by document.
translations.idiomatic: but since the Chongning era critics argued that the capital must be suppressed first and generally expedited execution by document.

sentences.zh: 振請復舊制。

translations.literal: Zhen asked to restore the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen asked to restore the old system.

sentences.zh: 詔捕亡命卒，得數千人，振請以隸步軍而除其罪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the capture of fugitive soldiers; several thousand were taken. Zhen asked to assign them to the Infantry and remit their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered fugitive soldiers captured; several thousand were taken. Zhen asked to assign them to the Infantry and remit their crimes.

sentences.zh: 步軍司欲論如法，振曰：「方多事之際，而一日殺數千人，必大駭觀聽。」

translations.literal: The Infantry Bureau wished to judge them according to law. Zhen said: "At a time of many troubles, to kill several thousand in one day would greatly alarm observers."
translations.idiomatic: The Infantry Bureau wished to judge them according to law. Zhen said, "At a time of crisis, to kill several thousand men in one day would greatly alarm the public."

sentences.zh: 乃盡釋之。

translations.literal: They were all released.
translations.idiomatic: They were all released.

sentences.zh: 改刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 金騎在郊，邀車駕出城，振為何栗言：「宜思所以折之之策。」

translations.literal: Jin cavalry were in the suburbs and demanded the imperial carriage leave the city. Zhen told He Li: "We should think of a strategy to rebuff them."
translations.idiomatic: Jin cavalry were in the suburbs and demanded the imperial carriage leave the city. Zhen told He Li, "We must devise a strategy to rebuff them."

sentences.zh: 栗不從。

translations.literal: Li did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: He Li would not listen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，及於難，年五十七。

translations.literal: Before long he met calamity at age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he met calamity at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 金人去，從子庭訪得其首歸葬之。

translations.literal: When the Jin departed his nephew Ting sought out his head and returned it for burial.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin departed, his nephew Ting recovered his head and brought it home for burial.

sentences.zh: 初，王黼使其客沈積中圖燕，振戒以後禍，積中懼而言不可。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Fu had his client Shen Jizhong plot for Yan; Zhen warned of future disaster and Jizhong, afraid, said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Fu had his client Shen Jizhong plot the Yan campaign. Zhen warned of future disaster, and Jizhong, afraid, said it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 既而振乃用是死，聞者痛之。

translations.literal: Yet in the end Zhen died for this very reason; those who heard grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end Zhen died for this very cause, and those who heard of it grieved.

sentences.zh: 初，宣和崇道家之說，振侍坐東宮，從容言：「孔子以《鴟鴞》之詩為知道，其詞不過曰'迨天之未陰雨，綢繆牖戶'而已。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Xuanhe the Daoist teachings were honored. Zhen attended the Eastern Palace and said calmly: "Confucius took the ode 'Owl' as knowing the Way; its words are no more than 'Before heaven has not yet darkened with rain, bind up the window and door.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Xuanhe era Daoist teachings were honored. Attending the Eastern Palace, Zhen said calmly, "Confucius took the ode 'Owl' as knowing the Way; its words are no more than 'Before the sky has darkened with rain, bind up the windows and doors.

sentences.zh: 老子亦云：'為之於未有，治之於未亂。

translations.literal: Laozi also said: 'Act when it does not yet exist; govern when disorder has not yet arisen.'
translations.idiomatic: Laozi also said, 'Act when it does not yet exist; govern when disorder has not yet arisen.'

sentences.zh: '今不固根本於無事之時，而事目前區區，非二聖人意。」

translations.literal: Now if we do not secure the foundation in a time without trouble but attend only to petty present matters, this is not the intent of the two sages."
translations.idiomatic: If we do not secure the foundation in a time of peace but attend only to petty present matters, this is not the intent of the two sages."

sentences.zh: 他日，太子為徽宗道之。

translations.literal: Another day the crown prince reported this to Emperor Huizong.
translations.idiomatic: Another day the crown prince reported this to Emperor Huizong.

sentences.zh: 徽宗寤，頗欲去健羨，疏左右近習，而宦寺楊戩輩方大興宮室，懼不得肆，因讒家令楊馮，以為將輔太子幸非常。

translations.literal: Huizong awoke and wished greatly to remove excess and distance close attendants, but the eunuch Yang Kai and his kind were then building palaces on a grand scale and feared they could not indulge freely; they slandered the household steward Yang Feng, saying he would assist the crown prince in an irregular fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong took the point and wished to cut excess and distance his close attendants, but eunuchs like Yang Kai were building palaces on a grand scale and feared they would lose their freedom. They slandered the household steward Yang Feng, claiming he would help the crown prince seize power irregularly.

sentences.zh: 徽宗震怒，執馮誅之，而太子之言亦廢。

translations.literal: Huizong was shaken with rage, seized Feng and executed him, and the crown prince's words were also abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong was furious, seized Feng and executed him, and the crown prince's counsel was abandoned as well.

sentences.zh: 振尹京時，兩宮方困於惎間，振極意彌縫，治龍德梁忻獄，寬其罪，不使有纖介可指。

translations.literal: When Zhen was Kaifeng prefect the two palaces were troubled by mutual suspicion; he did his utmost to mend matters, handled the Longde and Liang Xin case, lightened the offenses, and left no thread that could be pointed at.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen was prefect of Kaifeng the two palaces were troubled by mutual suspicion. He did his utmost to mend matters, handled the Longde and Liang Xin case, lightened the offenses, and left no fault that could be seized upon.

sentences.zh: 劉延慶

translations.literal: Liu Yanqing
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanqing

sentences.zh: 劉延慶，保安軍人。

translations.literal: Liu Yanqing was a man of Bao'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanqing was a native of Bao'an Army.

sentences.zh: 世為將家，雄豪有勇，數從西伐，立戰功，積官至相州觀察使、龍神衛都指揮使、鄜延路總管。

translations.literal: His family for generations were military men; bold and brave, he followed several western campaigns, won battle merit, and rose through offices to Tongzhou observation commissioner, commander of the Dragon and Divine Guard, and overall commander of the Fuyan route.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been military men for generations. Bold and brave, he took part in several western campaigns, won battle honors, and rose to observation commissioner of Xiangzhou, commander of the Dragon and Divine Guard, and overall commander of the Fuyan route.

sentences.zh: 遷泰寧軍節度觀察留後，改承宣使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner and observation regent of the Taining Army, then changed to commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner and observation regent of the Taining Army, then made a commissioner.

sentences.zh: 破夏人成德軍，擒其酋賞屈，降王子益麻党征。

translations.literal: He defeated the Xia at Chengde Army, captured their chieftain Shangqu, and received the surrender of the prince Yima Dangzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Xia at Chengde Army, captured their chieftain Shangqu, and received the surrender of the prince Yima Dangzheng.

sentences.zh: 拜保信軍節度使、馬軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commissioner of the Baoxin Army and deputy commander of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of the Baoxin Army and deputy commander of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從童貫平方臘，節度河陽三城。

translations.literal: He followed Tong Guan in suppressing Fang La and was military commissioner of the three cities of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Tong Guan in suppressing Fang La and served as military commissioner of the three cities of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 又從北伐，以宣撫都統制督兵十萬，渡白溝。

translations.literal: He again followed the northern campaign as pacification overall commander, directing one hundred thousand troops across the Bai Gou.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined the northern campaign as overall commander of the pacification forces, leading one hundred thousand troops across the Bai Gou.

sentences.zh: 延慶行軍無紀律，郭藥師扣馬諫曰：「今大軍拔隊行而不設備，若敵人置伏邀擊，首尾不相應，則望塵決潰矣。」

translations.literal: Yanqing marched without discipline. Guo Yaoshi seized his horse and remonstrated: "Now the great army moves in column without precautions; if the enemy sets an ambush, head and tail will not support each other and at the sight of dust they will break and flee."
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing marched without discipline. Guo Yaoshi seized his horse and remonstrated, "The great army is marching in column without precautions. If the enemy sets an ambush, the van and rear cannot support each other and the troops will break at the first sign of dust."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing would not listen.

sentences.zh: 至良鄉，遼將蕭幹帥眾來，延慶與戰，敗績，遂閉壘不出。

translations.literal: At Liangxiang the Liao general Xiao Gan led his host against him; Yanqing fought and was defeated, then shut the fort and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: At Liangxiang the Liao general Xiao Gan led his forces against him. Yanqing fought and was defeated, then shut himself in the fort and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 藥師曰：「幹兵不過萬人，今悉力拒伐，燕山必虛，願得奇兵五千，倍道襲取，令公之子三將軍簡師為後繼。」

translations.literal: Yaoshi said: "Gan's troops are no more than ten thousand; now he is exerting all strength to resist us and Yan Mountain must be empty. I wish five thousand picked troops to march by forced stages and seize it, with Your Excellency's son the Third General Jian leading the follow-up force."
translations.idiomatic: Yaoshi said, "Gan's troops number no more than ten thousand. He is exerting all his strength to resist us, so Yan Mountain must be empty. Give me five thousand picked troops to march by forced stages and seize it, with your son the Third General Jian leading the follow-up force."

sentences.zh: 延慶許之，遣大將高世宣與藥師先行，即入燕城，幹舉精甲三千巷戰。

translations.literal: Yanqing agreed, sent the great general Gao Shixuan with Yaoshi ahead, and they entered Yan city at once; Gan raised three thousand picked armored troops for street fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing agreed and sent the general Gao Shixuan with Yaoshi ahead. They entered Yan city at once, and Gan raised three thousand picked armored troops for street fighting.

sentences.zh: 三將軍者，光世也。

translations.literal: The Third General was Guangshi.
translations.idiomatic: The Third General was Liu Guangshi.

sentences.zh: 渝約不至，藥師失援敗走，世宣死之。

translations.literal: He broke the agreement and did not come; Yaoshi lost support, was defeated and fled, and Shixuan died.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi broke the agreement and did not come. Yaoshi lost support, was defeated and fled, and Shixuan was killed.

sentences.zh: 延慶營于盧溝南，幹分兵斷餉道，擒護糧將王淵，得漢軍二人，蔽其目，留帳中，夜半偽相語曰：「聞漢軍十萬壓吾境，吾師三倍，敵之有餘。

translations.literal: Yanqing encamped south of the Lu Gou. Gan divided troops to cut the supply route, captured the grain-protecting general Wang Yuan, and took two Han soldiers; he covered their eyes and kept them in the tent. At midnight he feigned conversation: "I hear a hundred thousand Han troops press our border; our army is triple theirs—more than enough for the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing encamped south of the Lu Gou. Gan divided his forces to cut the supply route, captured the grain escort general Wang Yuan, and took two Han soldiers. He blindfolded them and kept them in his tent. At midnight he feigned conversation: "I hear a hundred thousand Han troops press our border. Our army is triple theirs—more than enough to handle the enemy.

sentences.zh: 當分左右翼，以精兵沖其中，左右翼為應，殲之無遺。」

translations.literal: We should divide left and right wings, strike the center with picked troops, and have the wings respond—annihilate them to the last man."
translations.idiomatic: We should divide into left and right wings, strike the center with picked troops, and have the wings respond—we will annihilate them to the last man."

sentences.zh: 陰逸其一人歸報。

translations.literal: Secretly he let one escape to return and report.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly he let one man escape to return and report.

sentences.zh: 明旦，延慶見火起，以為敵至，燒營而奔，相蹂踐死者百余裏。

translations.literal: At dawn Yanqing saw fires rise, thought the enemy had come, burned the camp and fled; men trampled one another dead for more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Yanqing saw fires rise, thought the enemy had come, burned his camp and fled. Men trampled one another to death for more than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 自熙、豐以來，所儲軍實殆盡。

translations.literal: Since the Xi and Feng eras the stored military supplies were nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xi and Feng eras the stored military supplies were nearly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 退保雄州，燕人作賦及歌誚之。

translations.literal: He withdrew to hold Xiongzhou; the people of Yan composed fu and songs to mock him.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to hold Xiongzhou, and the people of Yan composed fu and songs to mock him.

sentences.zh: 朝議延慶喪師，不可不行法，坐貶率府率，安置筠州。

translations.literal: The court debated that Yanqing had lost the army and the law could not go unenforced; he was demoted to commandant of the Commandant's Office and settled at Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that Yanqing had lost the army and the law could not go unenforced. He was demoted to commandant of the Commandant's Office and settled at Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹知中國不能用兵，由是輕宋。

translations.literal: The Khitan knew China could not use troops and from this despised the Song.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan concluded that China could not wage war and from this despised the Song.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復為鎮海軍節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was again military commissioner of the Zhenhai Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again made military commissioner of the Zhenhai Army.

sentences.zh: 靖康之難，延慶分部守京城，城陷，引秦兵萬人奪開遠門以出，至龜兒寺，為追騎所殺。

translations.literal: In the Jingkang calamity Yanqing divided forces to defend the capital. When the city fell he led ten thousand Qin troops to seize the Kaiyuan Gate and break out; at Guier Temple he was killed by pursuing cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingkang calamity Yanqing divided his forces to defend the capital. When the city fell he led ten thousand Qin troops to seize the Kaiyuan Gate and break out, but at Guier Temple he was killed by pursuing cavalry.

sentences.zh: 光世自有傳。

translations.literal: Guangshi has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 論曰：靖康之變、執禮、振不忍都人塗炭，拒強敵無厭之欲，親逢其凶。

translations.literal: The commentators say: In the Jingkang transformation Zhili and Zhen could not bear to see the capital people suffer charcoal and ashes; they resisted the strong enemy's insatiable demands and personally met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: In the Jingkang transformation Zhili and Zhen could not bear to see the people of the capital suffer; they resisted the strong enemy's insatiable demands and personally met disaster.

sentences.zh: 熙靖、世勣不肯以一身事二姓，悲不食以終。

translations.literal: Xijing and Shiji would not serve two surnames with one body and died refusing food in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Xijing and Shiji would not serve two dynasties with one body and died refusing food in grief.

sentences.zh: 灌、延慶戰敗而沒。

translations.literal: Guan and Yanqing were defeated in battle and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Guan and Yanqing were defeated in battle and perished.

sentences.zh: 此數人者，其所遭不同，至於死國難則一而已。

translations.literal: These several men met different fates, yet in dying for the state's calamity they were one.
translations.idiomatic: These men met different fates, yet in dying for the state's calamity they were one.

sentences.zh: 雲之死，雖其有以取之，殆亦天未欲絕宋祀也；

translations.literal: Yun's death, though he had grounds to bring it on himself, was perhaps also because Heaven did not yet wish to end the Song sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: Yun's death, though he had brought it on himself, was perhaps also because Heaven did not yet wish to end the Song line;

sentences.zh: 不然，是行也，康王其危哉！

translations.literal: otherwise on that journey the Prince of Kang would have been in grave peril!
translations.idiomatic: otherwise on that journey the Prince of Kang would have been in grave peril!
